---
title: "Contribute"
description: "How to propose a workflow, a prompt, a skill or any other contribution."
---

Anyone can propose a contribution by filling in a short form on GitHub (a free GitHub account is needed). Every proposal is reviewed before it is published.

## How to propose

1. **Open the form** for your kind of contribution: [workflow](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=1-workflow.yml), [prompt](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=2-prompt.yml), [skill](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=3-skill.yml), [agent config](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=4-agent-config.yml), [model check](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=5-model-check.yml), [paper to review](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=6-review.yml) or [failure](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=7-failure.yml). You can also [see all the forms](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new/choose).
2. **Fill it in.** Required fields are marked; the list below says what each form asks for.
3. **Wait for the review.** A maintainer reads every proposal. If something is missing, the issue gets the label **needs-info** and a comment that says what: answer in a comment. When it is complete, it gets the label **ready**. Within a day it is turned into a page, and it is published as soon as a maintainer approves the page.

You do not need to know Git, Quarto or the structure of the site: the page is written for you, and you can comment on it before it is published.

## What each form asks for

- **Workflow:** goal, what you need, the steps with the prompts exactly as used, how to check the result, where it fails.
- **Prompt:** the prompt exactly as used, a real example of input and output, how to check the result, where it fails.
- **Skill:** what it does, the whole `SKILL.md` and any other files of the skill, how to check the result, where it fails.
- **Agent config:** what kind of project it is for, the whole `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, how to check the result, where it fails.
- **Model check:** the task, the prompt, the expected answer with the rule to mark a reply pass or fail, and the results for each model you tried.
- **Paper to review:** the published paper, whether it is open access, why it is worth a second review, and whether you could check the model's points. Reviews follow the [ground rules](reviews/index.qmd#ground-rules).
- **Failure:** the kind of error, what happened, the model that made it, how you caught it and the check that would have prevented it.

The forms for workflows, prompts, skills and agent configs also ask how you tested it: model, tool, date and the real case you ran it on (needed for L1). Every form asks for the authors to credit and your agreement to the licences.

## Catalogue numbers

When a contribution is published it gets a catalogue number: the letter of its type and the next free number, for example **AI W003** for a workflow or **AI P002** for a prompt. The number never changes, so you can use it to cite or mention the contribution.

## Credit and citation

Every contributed page shows its authors and ends with a **How to cite** box, with a ready-made reference and BibTeX entry built from the title, the authors, the date and the page address. Each page also keeps a **History** of its versions.

Contributions are published under the site licences: text under CC BY 4.0, code under MIT.

## Review criteria

- A colleague in the same field can follow the contribution and reuse it.
- Prompts are given exactly as used.
- *How to check the result* is concrete, not "verify the output".
- Nothing confidential or under embargo is included.

A contribution enters at **L1** when the author has tested it on a real case. It moves to **L2** when someone else reproduces it. Untested contributions are welcome too: they are published as **L0** drafts.

## Updating a contribution

A contribution keeps its catalogue number for life. [Open an Update form](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=8-update.yml) with its catalogue number when:

- you tested it again, with another model or on another date;
- you fixed or clarified a step, or improved a prompt;
- you found a new case where it fails;
- you reproduced it (L1 to L2) or checked it across models or dates (L3).

The update goes through the same review, and the page records it in its History. Whoever reproduces a contribution (L2) or rewrites a substantial part of it is added to its authors; smaller changes are credited in the History. When you cite a contribution that has been updated, give the date of the version you used: the catalogue number and the address stay the same.

If the method itself changes, propose a new contribution instead. It gets a new number and says *Supersedes AI W002* at the top, and the old page links to it.
